agents.brief: Build on founder's exp1/run.py (code blob 950bab3b5c2facef2e30586f62bd52733aa0b1bcb841fc41831a8ebd97287d52, exec exec-bfd076bd). Your goal: beat the position-aware GBM on CASP3_HUMAN_Roychowdhury_2020 and RASK_HUMAN_Weng_2022_abundance using 5-fold CV MAE (same KFold(5, shuffle, rs=0) protocol as run.py). Try added features: substitution-matrix (BLOSUM62) scores, per-position hydrophobicity profiles, ensembling with kernel ridge. Publish a finding with a prediction test only if MAE improves over the GBM in run.py, and cite exec ids for every number.

Audit founder's finding findin-a46858f0 (KCNE1 function, exec-bfd076bd). Check for leakage in run.py feats(): LOO position means, neighbourhood sums, and whether the CV protocol mirrors the evaluator's held-out setting (unseen variants at seen positions). Re-run variants with (a) no neighbourhood features and (b) non-LOO position means on train rows. If you find the reported gain is inflated, publish a correction or refutation with exec evidence. Report honestly whichever way it goes.

events.text: I need the lab's rules before planning anything. I'll read the guide, the help output, and the data layout first.
The guide was truncated in the middle, so I need the full contribution format and the baseline the evaluator compares against. I'll also read the dataset READMEs before choosing a research direction.
The baseline is one-hot (position × amino acid) with ridge regression. Before I choose a direction I need its code, the rest of the schema (especially the test fields), and the dataset sizes.

The baseline is one-hot position×AA with ridge. A stronger, cheap model should use position-level effects (leave-one-out), neighbourhood smoothing, and mutant-residue physicochemistry, fed to gradient boosting. I'll write one script that reports 5-fold CV against the baseline on all four DMS sets, with a prediction mode for the evaluator. I'll also print the `Test` schema I haven't seen yet.

The CV run beats the baseline on all four assays in the metrics, so I'll publish a `prediction` finding on KCNE1 function. Before that, I'll check that prediction mode runs on a fake held-out file, then store the code as a blob for the test.

The sanity check passed: prediction mode wrote 50 rows with the expected columns. The CV metrics beat the baseline on all four datasets, so I'll publish a `prediction` finding for KCNE1 function, using the exact numbers from exec-bfd076bd.

Extract the tar to get the founder's exact run.py, then read the feature code.

The founder's `feats()` builds training-row position means with leave-one-out, but `nb()` ignores the `loo` flag and `mt_mean` includes each row's own target. Leave-one-out target encoding is known to leak: within a position, LOO mean is a decreasing linear function of the row's own target, so trees can decode it. Test rows get a constant per-position mean, so this could inflate or distort CV. I'll write an audit script that reproduces the founder's number (`loo`), then ablates it: no neighbourhood features, non-LOO train means, out-of-fold encodings, and no position information at all. The founder's `exp1` has no recorded execs yet, so I'll build a self-contained `exp2/run.py` that reproduces the founder's GBM as a control. It adds BLOSUM62, a wild-type hydrophobicity window, and kernel-weighted per-position hydrophobicity and BLOSUM profiles (leave-one-out on train). It also fits kernel ridge and a 50/50 ensemble. I'll test it locally first, then run it through `lab exec` on both target datasets.

The full CV run finished. The ensemble has lower MAE than the founder's GBM on both datasets, and the stock GBM (`gbm_founder`) is the control. Next I'll get the exec id from `lab runs` and read the contribution schema.

The audit's main result is in. The founder's LOO features reproduce exactly (seed-0 MAE 0.1578), and the no-neighbourhood, non-LOO, and out-of-fold variants all keep a gain of roughly 21–26% over ridge.
